top_story: Trump’s threat in March to destroy Iran’s power infrastructure unless Tehran reopened the Strait of Hormuz sharpened a wider climate of coercion, with Iranian leaders answering by signaling readiness to widen confrontation across the region. In the weeks that followed, attacks on medical and rescue infrastructure in Lebanon intensified, with more than 120 rescue workers reportedly killed since March 2, deepening civilian vulnerability and eroding already fragile emergency services. Gaza’s more recent struggle to provide prosthetics and rehabilitation to amputees shows the same pattern in slower form: prolonged siege conditions are turning survivable injuries into permanent social and economic exclusion. The regional picture is one in which military pressure is no longer contained to battlefields, but is steadily degrading the civilian systems people depend on to survive, recover, and remain mobile.
